question: Where can I get a list of urban wastewater treatment plants in the United States, with location, design capacity, treated volume and treatment level?

answer.summary: EPA publishes two national structured sources. The Clean Watersheds Needs Survey 2022 (CSV/Access) lists about 16,450 records with a Treatment Plant type, with point location, design flow in MGD, effluent treatment level and NPDES permit numbers. ECHO (REST API) lists NPDES facilities with a POTW flag, coordinates, permit design flow and measured monthly effluent flow. They join by permit number. Florida DEP adds a state register with design and permitted capacity. Design flow definitions differ between sources, and plant-level treated volume is only available from monitoring reports.
main_caveats: CWNS is a voluntary 2022 snapshot: about 16,450 records have a Treatment Plant type while EPA's summary counts 17,544 POTWs; the difference is unreconciled.
ECHO rows are permits, not plants; use CWPFacilityTypeIndicator = POTW and join by permit number, and expect several permits at one site.
Design flow is not one measure: CWNS current and future flow, ECHO permit design flow and Florida design or permitted capacity differ; treated volume comes only from discharge monitoring reports.
ECHO queries over 100,000 rows are refused, so Florida, Georgia and Texas were not counted statewide.
EPA's CWNS bulk download is behind a popup with a usage-survey dropdown; table contents here were read from a third-party HydroShare copy.
Only Florida was tested among state registers; other states may publish capacity or treatment type that these sources lack.
answer.confidence_reason: Counts reproduced from EPA services and a CSV copy, with a three-way plant cross-check; definitions of design flow remain unreconciled and one state register was tested.

attributes.note: ECHO gives coordinates for all 16,996 POTW rows counted; CWNS has a point for 16,452 of 16,454 treatment plants; Florida DEP gives points.
Design flow in MGD: CWNS for 16,444 plants, ECHO for 76% of POTW rows, Florida design and permitted capacity. Population equivalent not published.
attributes.gap_note: Population-equivalent capacity was not found. ECHO design flow is blank for all Vermont POTW rows and for 4,041 of 16,996 counted rows. CWNS 'current design flow' behaves like current flow for Boothbay Harbor (0.29 MGD vs 0.64 MGD permit) and was not reconciled with permit design flow.

attributes.note: Measured monthly effluent flow exists in ECHO discharge monitoring reports per permit; one plant read (Boothbay Harbor, 24 months, 0.154-0.407 MGD).
attributes.gap_note: Only one plant's flow series was read; no bulk treated-volume list was tested. The facility-level 'actual average flow' field is blank on most rows and equals design flow on 22% of rows that have it, so it was not accepted as treated volume.

attributes.note: CWNS gives current effluent treatment level (Secondary 9,840, Advanced 6,187, Primary 87, Raw 1, NA 4) for 16,119 of 16,454 plants; ECHO and Florida have none.
attributes.gap_note: Fill rates were measured on a third-party copy of the 2022 files; EPA's own bulk download (popup-gated) was not completed. Snapshot of 1 January 2022.

key_fields.meaning: 11-digit facility identifier, infrastructure class (Wastewater, Stormwater, Decentralized Wastewater Treatment, Nonpoint Source) and Public/Private/Federal owner.
Facility types per record; 'Treatment Plant' marks plants. Other values include collection sewers, pump stations, biosolids, water reuse and desalination - WW.
Municipal, industrial, infiltration, wet-weather-peak and total flow in million gallons per day.
Raw, Primary, Secondary, Advanced or NA, plus disinfection flag; future level also given.
NPDES or non-NPDES permit number: the join key to EPA ECHO.

how_to_use.example_request: Open https://sdwis.epa.gov/ords/sfdw_pub/r/sfdw/cwns_pub/data-download, choose 'Nationwide 2022 CWNS Dataset' and 'Download CSVs' (a usage-survey dropdown appears first); the dictionary link on the same page downloads the XLSX directly.
how_to_use.example_result: CWNS ID 23000025001 (Boothbay Harbor WWTF, Maine, NPDES ME0100064): municipal flow current 0.29 MGD, future 0.64 MGD; effluent level Secondary; point 43.8508, -69.6322.
steps: Download the CSV tables and the dictionary.
Select FACILITIES with INFRASTRUCTURE_TYPE = 'Wastewater', then keep CWNS_IDs whose FACILITY_TYPES include 'Treatment Plant'.
Join FLOW (FLOW_TYPE = 'Total Flow' or 'Municipal Flow'), EFFLUENT, PHYSICAL_LOCATION (LOCATION_TYPE = 'Point') and FACILITY_PERMIT by CWNS_ID.
Join FACILITY_PERMIT.PERMIT_NUMBER to ECHO SourceID for permit status and monitored flows.
reading_traps: CURRENT_DESIGN_FLOW is not clearly a design capacity: for Boothbay Harbor it is 0.29 MGD, close to the plant's measured 2024 flow (0.288 MGD), while the 0.64 MGD permit design flow appears as FUTURE_DESIGN_FLOW.
In Maine, ECHO design flow equals CWNS current flow for 52 of 113 matched permits; the two measures are not interchangeable.
845 of 16,143 NPDES permit numbers are linked to more than one CWNS facility; a permit is not a plant.
The survey is voluntary and a 2022 snapshot; EPA's own count is 17,544 POTWs, against 16,454 records with a Treatment Plant type here (unreconciled).

problems: Only the XLSX data dictionary (38,625 bytes) was downloaded from EPA; the table downloads sit behind a popup with a required usage-survey dropdown, which returned HTTP 500 and 502 on first attempts and was not submitted.
Table contents were read from a third-party copy (source hydroshare-cwns-mirror) and not compared file by file with EPA's current files.
An earlier search summary suggested a dashboard URL; cwnsdep.epa.gov/2022dashboard redirects to the sdwis.epa.gov dashboard.

sources.adds: Live NPDES permit facilities with POTW/non-POTW indicator, coordinates, permit status, permit design flow and measured monthly effluent flow from discharge monitoring reports (DMR).
sources.summary: EPA ECHO serves every NPDES permit facility with a POTW flag, coordinates, permit status and design flow, and returns measured monthly effluent flow from discharge monitoring reports.
sources.coverage_note: United States. 16,996 POTW permit rows counted in 53 states/territories; 76% have a design flow and all have coordinates. Florida, Georgia and Texas need narrower queries.
caveats: Facility-level actual flow is often blank or equal to design flow; use the DMR series.

coverage.geographic: United States; 53 of 56 states/territories counted (FL, GA and TX exceed the 100,000-row query limit)

unit.value: One row per NPDES permit facility, not per plant; the same site can carry a POTW permit and several non-POTW (stormwater or general) permits at identical coordinates.

inclusion_rule.value: CWPFacilityTypeIndicator = 'POTW' marks publicly owned treatment works; 16,996 POTW rows were counted in 53 states/territories out of 833,392 permit rows.

reference_date.value: Live service on 2026-11-24; effluent chart read for 2024-2025.

update_frequency.value: Not stated on the pages read.

exclusions.value: Queries returning more than 100,000 rows are refused.
exclusions.quote: Rows Returned would be 108653. Queryset Limit would be exceeded - please make search parameters more selective.

key_fields.meaning: NPDES permit ID (for example ME0100064) and master permit for general-permit coverage.
Facility coordinates; the detailed report adds accuracy (for example 5 m or 30 m) and collection method.
Permit design flow (MGD); blank for many rows.
Facility-level 'actual average flow' (MGD); often blank and sometimes identical to design flow.
Effective, Expired, Terminated...; NPDES Individual Permit or General Permit Covered Facility.
Measured and limit values of effluent flow per monitoring period (parameter 50050 'Flow, in conduit or thru treatment plant').

how_to_use.example_result: Boothbay Harbor WWTF (ME0100064): monthly average effluent flow 0.154-0.407 MGD in 2024 (mean 0.288) against a 0.64 MGD limit; Maine list query returns 2,790 permit rows, 170 POTW, 153 with design flow.
steps: Call get_facilities with p_st and qcolumns, read QueryID, then get_download as CSV.
Keep CWPFacilityTypeIndicator = 'POTW'; treat CWPTotalDesignFlowNmbr as the permit design flow where present.
For measured volume call get_effluent_chart for a permit with parameter_code=50050 and read Average values.
reading_traps: Design flow is blank for all 93 Vermont POTW rows and 0 of 17 in Delaware; nationally 12,955 of 16,996 counted POTW rows (76%) have it.

CWPActualAverageFlowNmbr is present on 6,888 POTW rows and equals the design flow on 1,082 of the 4,820 effective-permit rows that have it, so it is not a reliable treated volume; the DMR series is the measured value.
Rows are permits: a site such as a large city plant also appears as several non-POTW stormwater permits at the same coordinates.
get_facilities refuses queries above 100,000 rows (FL, GA and TX by state); narrow by county or permit.

problems: Florida, Georgia and Texas statewide queries were refused (more than 100,000 rows), so national counts cover 53 of 56 states/territories.
Counts use CWPFacilityTypeIndicator = POTW as the municipal filter; the field's source definition was not read.
Effluent flow series was read for one plant only.

open_questions: Definition of CWNS CURRENT_DESIGN_FLOW versus permit design flow. Start: Boothbay Harbor (CWNS 23000025001 vs ECHO ME0100064) and the Maine match (52 of 113 equal). Next: read the CWNS technical documentation and compare more states.

EPA-hosted CWNS bulk download. Start: the download popup (usage-survey dropdown). Next: complete it from a browser and compare with the HydroShare copy, including the PHYSICAL_LOCATION correction of 2026-09-15.

Official count of 17,544 POTWs versus 16,454 CWNS records with a Treatment Plant type (16,394 public). Start: CWNS 2022 summary and FACILITY_TYPES. Next: test whether other facility types account for the gap.
ECHO counts for Florida, Georgia and Texas. Start: get_facilities refuses statewide queries. Next: narrow by county (p_co) or permit type.
Bulk treated volume: DMR flow for many plants. Start: get_effluent_chart for one permit (read). Next: test the ICIS-NPDES bulk download and measure how many POTWs report flow parameter 50050.

Other state registers (California, Texas, New York and others) and population-equivalent capacity. Start: Florida DEP layer as model. Next: search each state environmental agency for plant lists with capacity and process type.

history.note: Reproduced ECHO queries and an effluent chart, read CWNS tables from a CSV copy, and cross-checked two plants across sources. Effort level of the run was not independently known to the model.

National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System discharge permit; its ID (for example ME0100064) identifies the discharging facility.
Discharge Monitoring Report: periodic measured effluent values reported against permit limits.
Million gallons per day, the unit used for design and measured flow.
11-digit identifier of a facility record in the Clean Watersheds Needs Survey.
